front_line: The restaurant's operating system — and a toll on every check
thesis: Toast went deep on restaurants while rivals went broad, and that depth is becoming the industry's default operating system. Every module a restaurant adds is another root it has to tear out to leave, so the moat deepens as customers buy more. It's already profitable, with a shallow downside and large upside — an asymmetric setup with a hard catalyst nine weeks out.
moat: Genuine switching-cost moat on the customer; fragile and contestable on the take rate.
risks: Take rate is the most contestable variable and Square (equally scaled) could spark a price war.

categories.label: Moat
categories.note: Stickiness and switching costs, not a structural monopoly

categories.label: Risk
categories.note: Slower GPV per location, and ARPU drag. Competitors at heels

drafts.x_post: Toast ($TOST) is becoming the default operating system for restaurants — and the moat deepens with every module a customer adds. Profitable, asymmetric, and a dated catalyst on Aug 3. Dead Simple Score: 83/100. On the watchlist, buying a starter.
video_talking_points: Toast is the technology a restaurant runs on — payments, ordering, kitchen displays, payroll, online orders, all in one system.
Why now: it's profitable, earnings have beaten four quarters running with accelerating beats, and a hard catalyst lands August 3.
The bull point: every module a restaurant adds makes leaving harder, so the moat deepens as customers buy more.
The main risk: most revenue is thin-margin payment processing, and the per-check take rate is contestable if Square starts a price war.
The verdict: a watchlist name with real asymmetry — buy a starter, let August 3 confirm or kill it.
